# Devin Desktop hooks

This adapter supports only the Devin Desktop hook contract observed in the recorded Marketplace capability probe at [the harness capability floor](https://github.com/HarleyBartles/agent-asset-marketplace/blob/b481f98ae90aa45e5271d10fe1f7aaeb6c7047aa/skills/iterative-review/references/harness-capability-floor.md). That probe observed project-installed `.devin/hooks.v1.json` handlers and `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` payloads with `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`, and `hook_event_name`. The evidence is historical; verify the active Devin Desktop runtime before relying on it.

Do not use `--runtime devin-desktop` with Devin CLI. Its current [hook configuration](https://docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/hooks/overview) requires the standalone `.devin/hooks.v1.json` file to be a root event map, while this adapter renders the Desktop shape captured by the historical probe. The published CLI event example documents `session_id` and `prompt_id` but does not establish the per-call correlation ID this assessor needs. Add Devin CLI support only after its schema and correlation behavior have been separately verified.

The probe found no child `agent_id` in hook records. Its only supported child attribution was positional: capture one `run_subagent` dispatch at a time, with a matched start and completion, and attribute inner hook events between those boundaries. Concurrent dispatches or unidentified activity make child attribution ambiguous. The orchestrator and other agents must remain idle during the child dispatch; the orchestrator records this assumption with an explicit `--confirm-parent-idle --apply` self-attestation in the sanitized control log. Use the dispatch call ID as the `child:<dispatch-call-id>` selector. Devin Desktop's recorded `tool_response.success` and `tool_response.error` fields establish status when present. If the current runtime payload no longer matches these observed fields, stop and report unsupported runtime capability rather than guessing.

The public Devin CLI hook contract is documented separately and is not evidence for Devin Desktop behavior. Treat the Desktop runtime semantics here as recorded evidence, not as a vendor guarantee. Recheck the linked repository evidence and run a fresh live control when using a materially different Devin Desktop version.
